title: Tiered-fidelity MVP: conservative cuts for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: This ticket captures a scoped, tiered-fidelity approach to the Redwood Console MVP surface for dashboards, tracing, and cost breakdown. The goal is to ship a useful inspection surface within the next cycle while keeping unit-costs and telemetry retention budgets constrained. We propose conservative cuts and a progressive fidelity gating plan: implement a compact set of dashboard cards, a lightweight trace inspector focused on error funnels and tail latency, and a minimal per-route cost breakdown (no heatmaps or stream-level token attribution for GA). This ticket consolidates decisions from the PRD review, design sync, and infra feasibility calls and lists acceptance criteria for the trimmed MVP.
acceptance_criteria: Three dashboard card templates implemented and validated: Route Overview, Latency SLA, and Cost Summary
Trace inspector returns full flamegraph for a single span only when sampling=true; default view is aggregated error waterfall with top-5 traces
Per-route cost breakdown includes total tokens, 90th latency, and monthly spend estimate; excludes per-request token attribution and streaming token heatmaps
Client-side SDKs display aggregated route-level cost data via existing metrics endpoint; no new realtime socket required for MVP
Rollout gated by synthetic workloads: route card latency SLAs met for 95th percentile under baseline traffic (see perf-checklist link)
End-to-end telemetry retention for MVP is 7 days and instruments are validated to remain under infra quota during smoke runs
Docs/quickstart updated with one click onboarding flow and three example queries for troubleshooting
Product acceptance sign-off from Observability PM and Infra ENG lead recorded in PRD comments
decisions: Defer: per-request token attribution and token heatmaps to post-MVP; reason: high ingestion/storage cost and increased client complexity
Defer: full distributed trace span-search and arbitrary span detail views; reason: complex indexing and long-term infra cost
Keep: aggregated error waterfall and top-5 sampled traces for fast root-cause in the MVP
Keep: minimal per-route cost fields (tokens, latency, spend) to enable quick cost regressions alerting
Architecture: use existing metrics pipeline (Prometheus -> metrics-bridge) for dashboard cards and a lightweight trace sampler integrated with tracing-proxy for sampled spans
tradeoffs: User experience vs cost: limiting tracing detail speeds delivery but reduces forensic depth for hard incidents
Scope vs reliability: fewer features reduce surface area and risk for the GA but may require immediate follow-ups driven by support requests
Observability vs infra budget: retaining 7 days of trace samples allows debugging without committing to long-term storage costs
Developer velocity vs completeness: preferring composable card templates avoids bespoke cards but requires some customers to adapt existing workflows
